intro: Air traffic controllers make fast, high-stakes decisions that few other jobs demand. The closest of the 25 careers below is Power Distributors and Dispatchers, with a 70% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $106,730, which is 28% less than the $148,080 controllers earn.
why_it_works: A shift means tracking many moving aircraft, coordinating with pilots and other centers, and staying calm when plans change. O*NET rates judgment at 4.12 out of 5 for this job and complex problem solving at 4. Power dispatch, security analysis and compliance management share that focus on systems and risk. Your pay is already high, so most moves pay less. Several matches need a bachelor's degree.
tips: Check retirement and pension rules before you leave; timing can matter more than the next job.
Power grid dispatch uses the same real-time control skills and is your closest match.
Computer and Information Systems Managers are the only better-paid match, at $175,140, and usually need a degree.

faq.q: What jobs can former air traffic controllers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are power distributors and dispatchers (70%), Loss Prevention Managers (68%) and Compliance Managers (65%), based on O*NET 31.0. Information Security Analysts are 63% matched and earn $129,180, which is 13% less than the $148,080 controller median.

faq.q: Which careers for air traffic controllers pay more?
faq.a: Only 1 of the 25 matches pays more: Computer and Information Systems Managers earn $175,140, which is 18% more, according to BLS May 2025 data. Purchasing Managers earn about the same as controllers, at $148,080, with no change in pay.

faq.q: Do air traffic controllers need a degree to switch careers?
faq.a: Often yes. Only 11 of the 25 matches need no more education than controllers already have, and 4 of the top 10. A bachelor's degree is common in close matches, held by 55% of workers, so plan for coursework if you want management or security roles.

faq.q: What skills should air traffic controllers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are managing financial resources, negotiation, managing materials and repairing. Coordination already rates 3.88 out of 5 for controllers in O*NET, so business and budget skills are the main gap for management jobs outside aviation.
